text:
Mavrik Bourque finally scored his first goal as a Predator on November 25, and of course it came against Dallas, the team that drafted him 30th overall in 2020. He scored again two nights later against Utah. That ended a 19-game wait in a Nashville sweater.

The drought was mostly bad luck. He has 5.26 expected goals this season and just two goals, shooting 4.7% against a talent range closer to 12%. His shot rate is healthy (43 in 21 games), and his individual chance rate of 0.95 expected goals per 60 is higher than his Dallas numbers last year.

The concern is everything around his shot. Nashville has only 40.2% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, and his relative mark is more than nine points below his teammates. His minutes dipped to 11 and 12.8 a night during a mid-November stretch before climbing back to 18.4 against Utah. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 51% of his shots coming off the rush last season and an unusual 19% of his setups from behind the net. Watch whether his line can spend more time in the offensive zone.
